I've built LED lights before, but I was hoping to find a good, scientific breakdown of spectrum requirements and ratios during the different stages of the growth cycle. Does anyone know of any good books or websites that have some solid info?

Thanks!
I've decided to design an LED grow light and was hooping for some help...
I think its a mixture of blue & red, 3watt and 5watt diodes. Chip on board l.e.d. (cob) units r popular

I know that I could buy something, but the mad scientist in me likes making stuff. I already have good sources for LEDs, the mirocontroller and the MOSFETs for driving them.

I've found high powered LEDs to correspond with the following wavelengths:

Beta-carotene 450 nm and 480-485 nm (blue and different blue)

chlorophyll a 430 nm and 662 nm (blue and red)

chlorophyll b 453 nm and 642 nm (another blue and another red)

phycoerythrin 590 nm (amber/yellow)

phycocyanin 625 nm (red)

670nm and 700nm for the Emerson effect. (Really red and really, really freakin' red)

To cover all of these approximately, I have found sources for LEDs with the following wavelenghts:

430 nm - 440 nm @ 3W ea (Blue)

450 nm - 455 nm @ 3W ea (other blue)

460 nm - 470 nm @ 3W ea (different blue)

588 nm - 595 nm @ 3W ea (Amberlamps)

620 nm - 630 nm @ 3W ea (Red)

640 nm - 650 nm @3W ea (redder)

660 nm - 670 nm @ 1W ea (more red)

690 nm - 700 nm @ 1W ea (even more redder)

730 nm - 740 nm @ 1W ea (red that's better than reddit)

Many of the grow lights have set ups with 4 Reds (660 nm) to one blue (460nm). I was thinking that I'd be able to hit the peaks better with a wider variety of more targeted LEDs.

I was hoping that there'd be some information out there about the optimal ratios of wavelengths; and the timing/intensities required during cloning, vegetation and flowering stages.

I'll be able to run each different set of LEDs separately, so I have complete control over the on/off time, and intensities of each wavelengths.
